question: Will Chevron (CVX) Q3 oil-equivalent barrels per day net production (koebd) be above 4.1M?
rule: Company-reported worldwide Q3 2026 net oil-equivalent production, MBOED; YES only above 4.1M. Official Q3 earnings materials govern. Use range midpoint; most precise metric version wins. Metric absent when materials published or no materials by Nov30 2026 11:59 PM ET means NO.
facts: Q2 release Jul31: Q2 4,070 MBOED; Q1 3,858; Q2 2025 3,396; YTD26 3,965 vs YTD25 3,374. YoY growth attributed mainly to Hess, Permian and Gulf of America, partly offset by Partitioned Zone curtailments (Saudi Arabia/Kuwait). Historical actual, not Q3.

Aug7 Chevron “2026 Sensitivities and Forward Guidance”: full-year guidance 3,980–4,100 MBOED (+7–10% excluding asset sales), at $60/BBL Brent. Q3 upstream turnarounds/downtime impact estimated (150)–(200) MBOED; Guyana net entitlement expected to fall as Stabroek PSC cost recovery decreases Chevron net interest. Neither is a standalone Q3 worldwide total; do not mechanically add to Q2/annual guidance.

Sep8 CFO Barclays transcript: TCO performing “extremely well”; after earlier turnaround and six months testing, 3GP oil capacity raised 260→320 thousand b/d. Future debottlenecking expected incremental, not another similar step-change. Facility oil capacity, not worldwide net BOE/day/Q3 actual.

Oct6 Chevron announcement transfers Hess Midstream ownership/GP interests and DJ Basin crude-midstream assets, revises Bakken contracts; Chevron expects to sustain Bakken production via technology/operational improvements. Midstream/contract restructuring, not stated upstream production sale/Q3 volume. August guidance excludes asset sales.
